_comment: Synthetic demo-showcase scenarios, generation 2. These remain separate from data/scenarios.json and are optimized for selecting a live narrative scenario, not for changing official benchmark evidence. Customer Knowledge must still come from the RAG customer pack.

scenarios.probe: A Java web application built on a framework that evaluates OGNL expressions takes a request parameter and passes it into a server-side expression that is then evaluated. An attacker can submit a crafted expression that the server executes.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment-gateway Apache Struts web framework using OGNL expression evaluation
scenarios.expected_action: 24h SLA: page security on-call, open Sev-1, patch Struts or disable unsafe OGNL evaluation, and document PCI compensating controls within 4h.
scenarios.demo_goal: Backup v2 candidate. Uses S01 wording because Phase 3 handled S01 better than D01, while CK still retrieves payment-gateway tier-0/PCI facts.
scenarios.notes: Validated at 15/16 in the v2 evaluation sweep; only miss was Phase 3 priority becoming true instead of false.

scenarios.probe: The payment gateway has a Java request handler that places a request parameter inside an OGNL expression string and asks the framework to evaluate that expression on the server. A malicious expression can execute server-side behavior.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment-gateway Apache Struts request handler with OGNL expression evaluation
scenarios.expected_action: Treat as tier-0/PCI Critical: page security on-call, open Sev-1, patch the Struts expression handling path, and document compensating controls within 4h.
scenarios.demo_goal: Primary live candidate: clean 16/16 separation across Phase 1 through Phase 4 in the v2 evaluation sweep.
scenarios.notes: Validated 16/16: Phase 1 no SK/CK/action, Phase 2 CK-only, Phase 3 SK+CK+applicability without priority, Phase 4 full SK+CK+applicability+priority.

scenarios.probe: A Struts-based Java action constructs an expression-language statement from a request parameter and evaluates it as part of request processing. The attacker controls the expression contents and can make the server evaluate attacker-supplied behavior.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: Apache Struts action in payment-gateway expression-language evaluation path
scenarios.expected_action: Critical Sev-1 for payment-gateway: remove unsafe expression evaluation, deploy the Struts fix, and apply the 24h internet-facing tier-0 SLA.
scenarios.demo_goal: Second live candidate: clean 16/16 separation across Phase 1 through Phase 4 in the v2 evaluation sweep.
scenarios.notes: Validated 16/16 and useful as the immediate backup if E02 has live-run variance.

scenarios.probe: A card-authorization web flow evaluates an OGNL expression built from request data. A crafted request can change the expression so that the server evaluates attacker-controlled behavior during authorization processing.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment-gateway card authorization flow on Apache Struts
scenarios.expected_action: Open Sev-1, patch or disable unsafe OGNL evaluation, protect card authorization flows, and document PCI compensating controls within 4h.
scenarios.demo_goal: Business-context OGNL candidate; CK should make Phase 4 priority unambiguous.
scenarios.notes: Card-authorization wording may help CK retrieval for PCI and payment-gateway.

scenarios.probe: A payment-gateway admin screen searches the corporate directory by building an LDAP filter from a form value. Parentheses and wildcard characters in the input can alter the filter logic and return directory records outside the intended scope.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment-gateway admin tool querying corporate-directory LDAP filters
scenarios.ck_match: payment-gateway (tier-0, PCI) and corporate-directory (LDAP/AD; admin tool builds filters from form input)
scenarios.expected_action: Treat as Critical because the vulnerable admin path supports tier-0 payment-gateway operations; parameterize LDAP filters and open Sev-1.
scenarios.demo_goal: Learns from D06: keep the SK shape that Phase 3 got right, but add payment-gateway tier-0 context so Phase 4 can justify Critical.
scenarios.notes: Best non-OGNL candidate for a possible 16/16.

scenarios.probe: The customer portal login flow accepts a returnUrl parameter and redirects the browser there after authentication without checking that it is an allowed LatamPay destination. An attacker can send authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site.
scenarios.weakness_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
scenarios.affected_component_generic: customer-portal internet-facing login returnUrl redirect flow
scenarios.expected_action: High priority because the flow is internet-facing and part of the customer portal; restrict returnUrl to an allowlist of LatamPay domains.
scenarios.demo_goal: Learns from D07: keep the SK shape, but set expected priority to High because Phase 4 likely over-prioritized relative to Medium.
scenarios.notes: May produce Phase 4 Priority=True while Phase 3 remains Priority=False.

scenarios.probe: An employee administration page for payment operations concatenates a submitted username into an LDAP search filter. A crafted username can change the filter and cause the directory lookup to match broader privileged groups.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment operations admin page querying corporate-directory LDAP
scenarios.ck_match: corporate-directory (LDAP/AD) plus payment-gateway tier-0 operational administration
scenarios.expected_action: Open Sev-1 for the payment operations admin path; parameterize LDAP filters and add authorization checks before privileged group lookups.
scenarios.demo_goal: LDAP variant with clearer privilege escalation and payment operations context.

scenarios.probe: A Java MVC framework feature evaluates OGNL expressions during request binding. The application lets a request parameter influence the expression text, so a crafted request can make the server evaluate attacker-controlled expression behavior.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment-gateway Java MVC framework request binding using OGNL
scenarios.expected_action: Critical Sev-1: patch unsafe request binding, remove attacker-controlled OGNL evaluation, and document PCI compensating controls within 4h.
scenarios.demo_goal: A subtler OGNL variant that may keep Phase 1/2 weak while giving Phase 3 enough cues.
scenarios.notes: Use if E02/E03 are too easy for base Llama.

scenarios.probe: A settlement-processing service reconstructs Java objects from queue messages using native object deserialization. The message producer is upstream of the service, and the consumer does not enforce a class allowlist before object reconstruction.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: reconciliation-service settlement queue Java object deserialization
scenarios.ck_match: reconciliation-service (tier-1 money-movement reconciliation; serialized Java objects from settlement queue)
scenarios.expected_action: High priority due to tier-1 money-movement reconciliation; replace native deserialization with safe schema validation and class allowlists.
scenarios.demo_goal: Deserialization variant with more explicit ObjectInputStream/class allowlist language to help Phase 3 recover SK.
scenarios.notes: Backup if OGNL and LDAP are unstable.

scenarios.probe: A webhook sender accepts a merchant callback URL and performs the request from the server. The validation checks only the URL string prefix and does not resolve the final address, so crafted hostnames can still make the server request internal or link-local destinations.
scenarios.ck_match: notification-service (Cloud VPC; outbound webhooks to merchant URLs; cloud metadata endpoint reachable)
scenarios.expected_action: Critical: block metadata endpoint access, validate resolved destinations, restrict egress, and rotate potentially exposed cloud credentials.
scenarios.demo_goal: SSRF fallback that may be slightly harder for Phase 1 than D02 while preserving Phase 4 finish.
scenarios.notes: Use only if a CK-priority story is preferable to a pure SK story.

scenarios.probe: After customer login, the portal redirects to a next parameter supplied in the request. The application does not constrain the destination to LatamPay-owned hosts, so a crafted login link can send customers to an external domain after authentication.
scenarios.weakness_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
scenarios.expected_action: High priority: customer-facing login flow; enforce an allowlist of LatamPay-owned redirect destinations and monitor abuse.
scenarios.demo_goal: Open redirect variant designed to make Phase 4's likely High priority count as true.

scenarios.probe: A request parameter is inserted into an OGNL expression and evaluated by the Java web framework during request handling. An attacker can submit a crafted expression that changes server-side behavior during processing.
scenarios.affected_component_generic: payment-gateway Apache Struts OGNL request handling
scenarios.expected_action: Critical Sev-1 for payment-gateway: remove attacker-controlled expression evaluation and apply tier-0 PCI response requirements.
scenarios.demo_goal: OGNL variant with concise probe and CK cue in affected component only.
scenarios.notes: Tests whether keeping product details out of the probe makes Phase 1/2 weaker while preserving CK retrieval.
